note: Hand-maintained knowledge about every asset pack, the decisions already made about it, so they are never re-asked (CLAUDE.md 'Asset integration policy'). tools/assets/scan_packs.py reads this, measures every pack (files, sizes, frame grids, licence files, what was imported via game/assets/PROVENANCE.json) and writes docs/assets/ASSET_REGISTRY.md and data/asset_registry.json. Licence wording comes from the pack's own files or the page the owner supplied (ASSET_MANIFEST.md notes); 'storage' public = in the public repository, private = private-assets/ (git-ignored; only imported game files are committed). status: integrated (used in play), partial (some content used, more planned), planned (a task exists), reference (not for the game: tools, sources, docs), unused (reviewed; why in 'decision').

packs.name: Pixel Tileset: Village & Cave Expansion
packs.creator: Larchrow
packs.permissions: LICENSE.txt: royalty-free for commercial and non-commercial use in games, apps and videos; may be modified; credit appreciated, not required (credited anyway); may NOT be resold or redistributed as-is or as part of another asset pack or tileset. So the zip stays in private-assets and only the imported sheet is committed (owner decision B25R1-Q8, 2026-11-03).
packs.scale: 16 x 16 tiles on the world's own grid (no margin or spacing): 1:1. Its 32-colour larchrow32 palette is darker and outlined in near-black, a different look from Puny World; use pieces where the contrast reads (a well, a fence, props), not whole ground or walls beside Puny buildings.
packs.used_for: Imported whole as MapView atlas 5 (game/assets/tiles/larchrow_village_cave.png, tools/village_tile_sheets.py): tile value 500000 + Larchrow's tile_id (row * 16 + column), names in docs/assets/LARCHROW_TILES.md. Drawn (B25R1-014, Wilds.overworld_entries): a homestead claim's pen fence, fence_h / fence_v / fence_gate (the sides full height, their posts closing the corners: the sheet has no corner pieces), and a claim's finished well (tile 15, one tile; the part-built look is the Puny World sheet's dry ring, as Larchrow has no unfinished well).
packs.opportunities: Towns (region worker 3, region_stamps.json 'atlases'): timber and stone walls with window and door (500128-500133), red and blue roof Wang sets (500017-500031, 500033-500047, corner code TL 1 + TR 2 + BL 4 + BR 8; roof 00 empty), market stall 2x2 (500137-500140), signpost (500141), lamp post 1x2 (500144 top, 500145 bottom), lidded and water barrels (500146, 500147), crate of apples (500148), haystack (500016), stepping stones (500032), flower patches (500142, 500143), crops in 3 stages (500012-500014), tilled soil (500006, 500007), plank floor (500002-500005). Fences: fence_h, fence_v, fence_gate (500134-500136), no corner pieces. Caves: the cave wall/floor Wang set (500048-500063), animated lava (rows 4-7, 4 frames stacked by row), glowing crystals (4 frames, 500149-500152), stalagmites, mushrooms, iron and gold ore rocks (500157, 500158), bones, minecart rails, minecart, rope and ladder suit the planned skeleton caves (B14-09).
packs.known_issues: tile ids 64, 80, 96 and 112 are unnamed (lava set's plain floor column, frame rows): see tile_index.csv. Only the 16 px sheet is imported; the 48 px copy, Tiled and Godot files are not needed.

packs.name: Grass Pack
packs.creator: Yavuz (arsden)
packs.permissions: CC0 (owner, itch.io page): no restriction. Kept in private-assets only because the owner supplied it there.

packs.name: FREE - Cozy Village RPG
packs.creator: kassuii
packs.permissions: Free version (owner's screenshot of the terms): usable in free and commercial projects, may be modified; credit not required but appreciated (credited anyway); may NOT be used to train AI (we do not); may not be resold or redistributed, even modified. Original .rar (private-assets/FREE - Cozy Village RPG.rar) extracted byte for byte with unar into the folder; only imported pieces would be committed.
packs.scale: Measured: ATLAS_FREE.png (1800 x 900) is drawn at 3 screen px per art pixel (every run of colour a multiple of 3), so 1/3 nearest gives its native 600 x 300 at the world's density (its ground tiles 32 x 32 native = 2 x 2 world tiles). TREES_OAK.png (1024 x 321) is native 1:1, each oak about 128 x 128 px: 8 world tiles wide, only reducible by 2 with detail lost.
packs.decision: Looked at beside Puny World grass, flowers, rocks and bushes at the game's zoom (agent decision, 2026-11-03): its palette is darker and more detailed. The three tall flowers (white, yellow, red) and the two grey stones sit well at 1/3; the bushes (dark, heavy), the slate-roofed houses and window box (a building style no stamp uses), the raised grass, floors and pond (another ground set) clash and are not used; the oaks are too large for the world's trees and not integer-reducible without losing their detail. Nothing is imported until a system draws those pieces (a pack counts as integrated only when used).
packs.opportunities: Wildflower variety (the three tall flowers, 1/3 nearest) and loose stones (1/3) for the overworld's flower and rock decoration, as extra variants by a fixed hash of the cell.
